A little help connecting

Make yourself at home.

From finding your TV to picking up where you left off. Here is what you need to get Roomote connected.

Find your answer

First-time setupCompatibilityTroubleshootingContact support

Your first connection

  1. Turn on the TV. Connect your Android phone to the same reachable home network as the TV.
  2. Open Roomote and tap the TV icon at the top right. Choose a discovered TV. You can also enter its IP address from the TV's network settings.
  3. Start pairing. Enter the current six-character code shown on the TV, including any letters.
  4. Once connected, the TV icon shows a green indicator. Try the directional pad, OK, Home, and Back.

Roomote remembers your successful connection and tries to reconnect to that TV when the app opens or returns to the foreground. Open the TV icon to switch TVs, retry, disconnect, or forget a TV.

No developer mode needed. You do not need to enable ADB, USB debugging, or install a Roomote companion app on the TV.

Will my TV work?

You need an Android phone running Android 8.0 or newer and a TV that provides the compatible Android TV Remote Service v2 protocol. Android TV Remote Service app version 5 or newer is the intended target.

Many Android TV and Google TV devices provide this service. A model name or Android version alone does not guarantee support. Older Remote Service v1 devices and Android boxes without Google's compatible remote service are not supported.

Roomote does not support Fire TV, Roku, Samsung Tizen, or LG webOS. It does not provide infrared or Bluetooth control, voice input, a text keyboard, screen mirroring, or media casting.

The phone and TV must be able to reach one another on the same local network. Ethernet-connected TVs can work when connected to the same router as the phone's Wi-Fi. Cellular data alone cannot reach your home TV.

A few things to try

My TV does not appear in the list.

Make sure the TV is awake and both devices share a reachable local network. Tap Scan again in TV settings. Guest Wi-Fi, client isolation, VPNs, and blocked multicast discovery can prevent a TV from appearing.

Try entering the TV's current IP address manually. If that also fails, check that Android TV Remote Service is installed and enabled, and that the TV supports the v2 protocol.

I'm using a phone hotspot or USB tethering.

Tethering does not by itself put the TV and phone on a reachable shared network. Connect the TV to the phone's hotspot, or connect the phone and TV to the same router. Whether hotspot clients can communicate with the host or one another depends on the phone's network configuration.

Discovery may be unavailable on some hotspot setups. Manual IP entry can help only when a direct network route to the TV exists.

The pairing code does not work.

Use the current six-character code displayed by the selected TV. Include letters as well as numbers; a code from an earlier attempt may have expired. Cancel the pairing and start again if needed.

If no code appears, check the TV's Android TV Remote Service version and available TV or service updates.

Roomote stopped reconnecting automatically.

The TV may be asleep, its address may have changed, or it may have forgotten the phone. Open the TV icon, rediscover the TV, and connect. Pair again if requested.

Roomote makes one automatic attempt per opening or return to the foreground. It does not continuously retry an unreachable TV. After you choose Disconnect, it stays disconnected for that app session. Forgetting the last used TV also clears the automatic selection.

Some remote buttons do nothing.

Try Home or a directional key first. Volume, input, playback, and menu behavior depend on the TV firmware, the active TV app, and any external audio system. Roomote sends the key press, but the TV decides how to handle it.

I can turn the TV off, but not on.

A TV in deep standby may switch off its network service. Roomote can send a power key only while that service is reachable. Check the TV's supported network or standby settings. The app cannot power on an unplugged TV.

What is the difference between Disconnect and Forget TV?

Disconnect closes the current connection and keeps the saved TV for later. Forget TV removes the saved TV and its trusted certificate from Roomote. You will need to pair again to control it.

Forgetting a TV in Roomote does not remove the phone from the TV's own list of paired devices. Use the TV's settings to revoke the phone there if needed.

Do I need an account, subscription, or internet connection?

No Roomote account, subscription, purchase, or advertisement is required. Remote commands use the local network directly and do not pass through a Roomote cloud service. The TV's streaming apps and system services may separately need internet access.
